text: CargoFlow's cargo notes plugin gives the MetaMask Agent Wallet a new trading superpower: evidence-aware credit trading on Monad.
An agent can find, price and buy Cargo Notes: short-dated trade-finance positions, priced by the cargo's own sensor evidence.
It's a native mm plugin. Install it once, and the agent gets six new commands.
mm cargo list reads the whole market from Monad: status, evidence score, claim, on-chain mark, ask and best bid for every note.
mm cargo quote explains a price in plain words.
This note is paused after a temperature excursion. Its evidence score is forty-eight, so the drawn leg is marked down, and down again while it's paused.
So when the agent is asked to buy it, the plugin refuses before anything is signed.
Paused, evidence below the minimum, ask above the mark. Nothing reaches the wallet.
mm cargo scan is the strategy command. It checks every note against your rules and your budget, and explains each decision.
Right now nothing qualifies, so nothing is bought.
Earlier, a note was offered one percent under its mark, with a perfect evidence score. The agent bought it.
Two transactions: an exact USDC approval, then the buy. MetaMask held each one until the owner approved it by email.
Both landed on Monad: the approval, and the buy, for about three USDC.
The agent wallet is now the note's financier of record. When the importer pays, it receives principal plus fee.
And the trading page's market feed, indexed by Envio, shows the fill.
Two layers keep this safe. The plugin enforces evidence, price and budget rules.
MetaMask's Guard mode adds allowlists, an outflow limit and two-factor approval on every transaction.
A skill file teaches any agent to plan first, explain refusals, and never loosen a limit to force a trade.
And we made Agent Wallet work on Monad testnet. The plugin sends its own gas and fees, and loads the host's SDK.
Cargo notes for MetaMask Agent Wallet. Evidence-aware credit, traded by agents, on Monad.
CargoFlow's Cargo Note market runs on Envio HyperIndex, reading Monad testnet through HyperSync.
One config indexes three contracts: the note market, the financing controller and the evidence registry, from the deployment block.
Handlers turn every ask, bid, trade and transfer into entities: notes, trades, order events and market stats.
It's deployed on Envio Cloud, synced to the chain head, behind a public GraphQL endpoint.
Now, end to end. With the trading page open, we raise a bid on a note, on chain.
The transaction is mined in about two and a half seconds. A second and a half later, HyperSync has delivered the log, and HyperIndex has written it.
The GraphQL endpoint already returns the new bid, with its price and the note's evidence mark.
And the page's market activity feed shows it on its next refresh, about seven seconds after we sent it. Three bids now.
Here is the same transaction on MonadVision.
Envio gives traders the full history of every note, live, from Monad.
CargoFlow's hosted API runs on Alchemy's Monad testnet RPC, as its primary endpoint.
The health check says it: RPC, primary. The service logs show the Alchemy endpoint, with Monad's public RPC as the fallback.
Behind it is a failover client. Alchemy goes first. If it's unreachable, errors, or rate-limits, traffic moves to the fallback, and returns on its own after a cooldown.
Reverts never trigger a failover, so behaviour stays deterministic.
Alchemy's free tier allows ten-block log queries on Monad, so the indexer reads ten blocks at a time. That's about two and a half calls a second.
Every chain read, evidence commit, milestone release and pause goes through Alchemy.
So the shipment dashboards, the evidence-gated money and the Cargo Note market all run live on Monad, through Alchemy.
CargoFlow, on Monad, powered by Alchemy.
Your loan is stuck at sea.
Until the cargo speaks for itself.
Now it trades.
Cargo Notes. CargoFlow, on Monad.
